run: architecture candidate 8: arm A+ reads the app's rules; arms A and A+ on the dev set before (a2c5dad) and after (63569f3), synthetic known answers (validation/__tests__/aplusRules.test.js), 2026-10-19
evidence: Candidate 8 (docs/AGENT_PLAN.md, sections B and E): arm A+, the model-free control, applied three rules of its own where the app has one, so B - A+ partly measured a disagreement between A+ and the app rather than the model. (1) Split site: A+ used arm A's rule (PC1/PC2 >= 1.3, PC1 resolved, kappa1 <= -0.5) with delta = sqrt(rms1^2 - rms2^2); the app's is isSplitSite (PC1 resolved, kappa1 <= -0.5 and at least 3 sampling errors sqrt(24/n) below zero) with list_sites' delta = sqrt(rms1^2 - rms_perp^2). Evidence for the app's: on synthetic prolate Gaussian sites (no split) arm A's rule called 3.6 % split at 216 copies and 14 % at 100 copies (2,000 seeds each), isSplitSite none; a planted +-0.15 A split over a 0.05 A width at 216 copies is found by both (isSplitSite in 300 of 300 seeds, its delta within 1.96 errors in 94 %); rms2 alone biases delta low (ai-assistant.md Step 20). On dev, dev-jahn-teller's F sites 5 and 6 (kappa1 -0.95 and -0.93 at 216 copies, z -2.84 and -2.78) are split by arm A's rule but not by the app's, the price of the false-positive control; the F claim (the site with the largest delta) is unchanged. (2) Cluster elements: A+ tried every same-element first shell peaking below 3.6 A; the evidence gate tries an element whose own first shell holds 0.5-4.5 neighbours (CLUSTER_CN_MAX). Physics: dimers (CN 1), trimers (2), tetrahedra (3) and octahedra (4 per member) are finite clusters, CN 6-12 a network; a distance cut tries networks and misses long clusters. On dev the CN rule tries exactly the planted V2 dimers, Mo3 triangles and the F around Cu (CN 4); the eight elements the 3.6 A rule also tried (the O of four perovskites, CN 8; FeSi's Fe and Si, CN 6; rock-salt Mg and O, CN 12) are extended networks the cluster engine itself refuses. Neither rule tries a cluster whose members have 5 or more like neighbours (an icosahedron): a limit both the gate and A+ now share. (3) Lower group's tolerance: A+ read the space group at the sampling noise floor; measure_symmetry_lowering's default and the Workbench's tolerance question use 1.25 x the floor. No dev group moves (every rung below the true group ends below 0.7 x the floor, every true group holds past 1.25 x it); the cost is that a lowering whose group holds only to 1-1.25 x the floor is not read (a synthetic 0.0147 A shift, holding to 1.18 x, reads Pm-3m; 0.027 A, 2.2 x, reads P4mm). No dev case shows the margin wrong, so the app's rule is taken. Arms A and A+ on the dev set before and after: every arm A and D record identical (arm A's rules are the frozen protocol's and unchanged); every score and claim identical except dev-offcentre's delta, 0.201 -> 0.202 A (planted 0.2); all ten A+ records move in their readings (the group read at 1.25 x the floor, the same group everywhere; list_sites split readings with kappa1, z and delta; eight network cluster readings gone; dev-jahn-teller's F sites 5 and 6 no longer split) and are re-recorded in validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json. The test set was not run. The model-visible snapshots are unchanged, so PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 2026-10-19.8. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
proposed_fix: A+ calls the app's functions, held in SWEEP_RULES (validation/armA.js) and tested to be the app's own: isSplitSite and splitDisplacement for the split site (appSplitSites, its readings on page list_sites); clusterElementsOf (llm/context/shells.js, which now holds CLUSTER_CN_MAX; evidence.js imports it and re-exports the constant) for the cluster elements; lowerGroupTolerance (llm/context/runContext.js: NOISE_FLOOR_MARGIN x symmetryNoiseFloor, 2 digits, 0.025 A without counts) for the group A+ reads and the shift tool's lower group, NOISE_FLOOR_MARGIN replacing copilotTools.js' own copy and clarify.js' NOISE_MARGIN. Arm A is unchanged. The skill lint gains a rule check (RULES) and five allow-list entries for the skill sentences that state these rules otherwise (displacement-anisotropy SKILL.md:27 and significance-reading.md:17, coordination-shells SKILL.md:51, local-symmetry SKILL.md:38 and :59); the skill text is the user's and waits for the skill review (plan 5.3). A+'s own joining rules stay (one claim per element, a mode explains its element's split sites, an off-centred centre its own split shell, a mode's polarisation from the most prolate site's PC1 at PC1/PC2 >= 1.3: the app has no polarisation rule). Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19; the user may reverse it.
